criteria.reasoning: The memo correctly computes program expenses as $19,066,000 less $14,180,000, or $4,886,000. But it computes the denominator as $20,515,000 less only $14,180,000, calling the result $6,335,000; the criterion requires removing all $14,275,000 of gifts in kind, for a denominator of $6,240,000.

The memo reports the program expense ratio as “77.1%” and calculates it as “$4,886,000 ÷ $6,335,000.” The criterion requires 78.3% ($4,886,000 ÷ $6,240,000), so the memo reports a different figure as the policy ratio.
The memo reports the program expense ratio as 77.1% against an 80.0% or higher target and explicitly says “Not met.” It therefore tells the committee the target was not met in 2025.

The memo subtracts “$600,000” for the “bequest — Estate of Harriet M. Okafor” from contributions used in the indicator. It explains that “the policy removes every bequest and estate distribution from the denominator because bequests are non-recurring,” so the criterion is satisfied.

The memo's table gives contributions for the indicator as $3,985,000, calculated from $18,930,000 less $14,345,000 in noncash contributions and the $600,000 bequest. This matches the criterion's required denominator.
The memo reports “$866,300 ÷ $3,985,000 = $0.217, reported as $0.22.” This matches the required cost to raise a dollar of $0.22.

The memo lists the cost-to-raise-a-dollar target as “$0.20 or less” and explicitly says “the indicator is **met**,” because it is within the $0.25 threshold. The criterion requires the memo to say the $0.20 target was not met, so this fails.

The memo starts its operating-reserve calculation with “Total net assets, Part X line 32, end of year | $7,852,000.” The criterion explicitly says this fails if the memo starts from total net assets rather than the $6,612,000 without donor restrictions.

The memo reports the operating reserve as “$2,744,000,” calculated from total net assets less fixed assets. The criterion requires $1,504,000 using net assets without donor restrictions less fixed assets and explicitly fails any other figure.

The memo states annual operating expenses as “$5,794,000” after subtracting depreciation and gifts in kind expensed. It also gives monthly operating expenses as “$482,833,” which matches the criterion.
The memo reports “5.7 months” of operating reserve, while the criterion requires 3.1 months and explicitly says reporting 5.7 fails. The criterion is not satisfied.
The memo reports the operating reserve as 5.7 months against a target of 3.0 months or more and explicitly states it was “Met.”

The memo states, “The program expense ratio is down from 81.6% in fiscal 2024.” No fiscal 2024 program expense ratio appears in the reference files or can be computed from the figures they provide. The criterion explicitly treats an unsupported prior-year ratio as a failure.
